Dominant Segments: Office workers; bazaar shoppers; some tourists
Notable Communities: Azerbaijani majority; Russian-speaking; smaller Iranian and Turkish shopper mix at Taza Bazaar
Age Life Stage Skew: 30s-50s workers and families; mixed-age market visitors
Student University Proximity: None nearby; 28 May is a transit hub not a campus
Day Night Pattern: Daytime bazaar and office peak; quieter residential evenings
Product Recommendations: Taza Bazaar lamb and offal; smoked Caspian fish; village qatıq and pendir; tandir bread; Badamlı/Sirab; sunflower seeds
Summary: This is the original Wolt Market Baku catchment around 28 May and Taza Bazaar. Range bazaar heroes (meat, fish, dairy, dried fruit) rather than Port Baku gourmet. Treat it as the city's traditional grocery heart, not as Yasamal students or Landmark tourists.

Notable Communities: Azerbaijani majority; student mix including regions of Azerbaijan; some international students at BSU
Age Life Stage Skew: Late teens-20s students; 30s-40s families in Yeni Yasamal
Student University Proximity: Baku State University and several institutes along Zahid Khalilov
Day Night Pattern: Campus daytime; evening shared-flat cooking and late convenience
Dietary Considerations: Halal is default; student vegetarian emerging
Product Recommendations: Value bread and qutab; Yeni Yasamal produce; Jalə juices; affordable chicken; ready-to-cook dolma/plov kits; energy drinks
Summary: Yasamal is Baku's student and inner-west family belt around Wolt Market Yasamal. Prioritise value, ready-to-cook national dishes and bazaar produce. Do not copy Landmark's wine and specialty-coffee depth here.

Notable Communities: Azerbaijani professionals; Russian-speaking; tourist mix around Fountain Square and Icherisheher
Day Night Pattern: Office-heavy weekdays; tourist traffic all day around Nizami Street
Dietary Considerations: Halal is default; some imported vegetarian demand
Product Recommendations: Specialty coffee beans; Savalan wine and distillates; tandir bread; Port Baku deli; Jalə pomegranate; gift pakhlava
Summary: Landmark (Nizami 92 / Sabayil) is the downtown premium store. Range specialty coffee, Azerbaijani wine and gift pantry. Bazaar volume protein belongs in Baku and Nasimi, not here.

Notable Communities: Strong Azerbaijani majority; fewer short-stay expats than downtown
Day Night Pattern: Residential day and evening; weekday industrial-area peaks
Product Recommendations: Family-pack lamb and chicken; value bread; Sirab water; everyday veg; sunflower seeds; large-pack staples
Summary: Binagadi is northwest Baku's working-family catchment. Range volume staples and bazaar protein. Skip Landmark wine, White City coffee and tourist tandir kits.

Dominant Segments: Khatai families; White City new-build professionals
Notable Communities: Azerbaijani majority in Khatai housing; more mixed professional in Ağ Şəhər
Day Night Pattern: Residential evenings in Khatai; cafe and after-work demand in White City
Product Recommendations: UCB/SENSUM beans; Beerbaşa; Goygol brandy; split fruit (value veg + White City fruit); family chicken
Summary: Khalglar sits between Soviet Khatai housing and White City. Dual-range: value family grocery plus a short premium coffee/wine set for Ağ Şəhər. Do not treat the whole catchment as Landmark.

Notable Communities: Azerbaijani majority; Russian-speaking; dense mixed inner-Nasimi

Day Night Pattern: Daytime market and school-run; evening family cooking
Product Recommendations: Nəsimi bazaar produce and meat; village dairy; tandir bread; Sirab; family meal kits
Summary: Wolt Market Nasimi (Imran Qasimov) is residential Nasimi, not the Taza Bazaar tourist edge. Range family grocery and local dairy. Overlap with the Baku store is real — differentiate by everyday packs versus bazaar specialists.

Dominant Segments: Regional capital families; university students; west-Azerbaijan shoppers
Notable Communities: Azerbaijani majority; some Russian-speaking; shoppers from surrounding rayons
Spending Profile: Mid-range (below Baku Landmark; above village shops)
Student University Proximity: Ganja State University and several institutes in the city
Day Night Pattern: Daytime bazaar and high-street; evening family cooking
Product Recommendations: Village qatıq and pendir; tandir bread; local lamb; Sirab/Badamlı; value coffee not Port Baku wine
Summary: No live Wolt Market store yet. Ganja is Azerbaijan's second city and the natural first expansion test outside Baku: family grocery, university value, and west-region produce. Do not copy Landmark's tourist wine set. Use national AZE trends (village dairy, ready-to-cook dishes) as the starting hypothesis, then list Ganja producers before opening.

Summary: No live Wolt Market store yet. Sumqayit is the industrial satellite of Baku and a volume family grocery city. Range like Binagadi, not like Landmark. Useful as a same-metro expansion once Baku catchments are stable.

Summary: No live Wolt Market store yet. Mingachevir is a mid-size interior city. A first store would be family grocery plus a short national-dish kit set, not Baku specialty coffee.

Summary: No live Wolt Market store yet. Lankaran is the southern produce capital. A dark store here should own citrus, rice and Caspian-south fish rather than Baku White City coffee.

Summary: No live Wolt Market store yet. Nakhchivan is an exclave — logistics, not just ranging, is the constraint. Treat it as its own supply island; Baku producer lists will not transfer 1:1.
